item.title: Nationwide refining capacity surges as Baiji ramps up
item.description: Iraq can now process over 1.5 million bpd of crude, as the country's largest refinery completes a decade-long comeback.

item.title: Iraqi oil shutdowns loom as U.S. attacks Iran
item.description: Some production is already offline and Iraqi oil officials are bracing for a total loss of southern exports.

item.title: Damascus moves to centralize control over Syrian oil sector
item.description: Kurdish-led authorities in northeast Syria are losing their hold on the country’s largest oil fields as foreign investors look for opportunities.

item.title: Iraq begins nationwide production shutdowns
item.description: With exports halted by war, Iraq has limited options to keep fields operating and has begun taking millions of barrels of daily production offline.

item.title: Oil field attack signals dire war risks for Kurdistan energy sector
item.description: Drone strikes on Sarsang raise new doubts for IOCs about the viability of restarting wartime oil production as the KRG demands security guarantees from Baghdad.

item.title: Oil companies evacuate as Burjisiya drone attack highlights rising threat
item.description: Strike on a key oil logistics hub in Basra signals danger for southern Iraq's oil sector as Iran and its proxies target U.S. companies.

item.title: Basra tanker attack marks deepening crisis for Iraq oil sector
item.description: Iraq is facing a widening array of security threats and economic consequences from the Iran war.

item.title: Northern exports stalled by Baghdad-Erbil disputes
item.description: With southern oil exports choked off by war, Baghdad cannot use its only backup pipeline route because of a fight with the KRG over customs revenue control.

item.title: Northern pipeline restart offers limited relief
item.description: A political breakthrough unlocks Iraq's only secondary pipeline export outlet, but volumes are capped by infrastructure constraints and security threats.
